name: Methasterone

lead: Methasterone is a lab-made oral steroid that was sold as a bodybuilding supplement called Superdrol in the 2000s. It was never approved as a medicine.
No human trial has measured its effect on muscle. Claims of fast gains come from forum logs and animal-based assumptions, while published human reports are mostly of liver and kidney problems.

paras: It is an androgen-receptor agonist derived from dihydrotestosterone, with a 17-alpha methyl group that lets it work when swallowed. Animal assays suggest a high anabolic-to-androgenic ratio, but this has not been tested in humans.

Case reports describe cholestatic jaundice, kidney injury and hospitalisation, and a supplement cluster in New York involved liver damage. Users also report suppressed testosterone, gynecomastia and lipid changes. It is a controlled substance in the US and banned in sport.

lead: Methasterone (2alpha,17alpha-dimethyl-5alpha-androstan-17beta-ol-3-one, also called methyldrostanolone) is a synthetic, orally active anabolic-androgenic steroid derived from dihydrotestosterone. It was never approved as a medicine. In the 2000s it was sold in the United States under the brand name Superdrol as an over-the-counter bodybuilding supplement and was described by sellers as a prohormone, although forum users and laboratory studies have treated it as an active steroid itself [1][2][3].

No clinical trial of methasterone in humans for muscle gain or any other purpose has been published. Human information consists of case reports of cholestatic jaundice and kidney injury in users, forensic analyses of supplements, and anti-doping metabolism studies [4][5][6]. It is a controlled substance in the United States and is on the World Anti-Doping Agency prohibited list [7][8].
infobox: Controlled substance in the US (Schedule III, per a 2023 analysis) [8]

paras: Methasterone has no medical indication. It has been taken by bodybuilders and recreational lifters to gain muscle and strength. T Nation posters from the mid-2000s described rapid gains of lean mass and tested it in training logs, while others raised concerns about side effects [9][10]. Users on looksmax.org compare it with other oral steroids such as oxandrolone (Anavar) and trenbolone-related compounds when talking about getting muscular [11][12].

As an androgen, methasterone is understood to act on the androgen receptor. The 17alpha-methyl group is a structural feature shared with other oral anabolic steroids that slows hepatic breakdown and permits oral use; the same class feature is linked to liver effects [3][13]. Preclinical claims of a high anabolic-to-androgenic ratio come from animal assays and have not been confirmed in human trials [3].

Anti-doping research has studied its metabolism using human liver microsomes and chimeric mice carrying human hepatocytes, because trials of designer steroids in humans are ethically restricted. These studies found that dimethazine, an azine-linked dimer of two methasterone molecules, degrades to methasterone, and that products labelled as methylstenbolone have also contained methasterone [14][15][15]. Other laboratory papers have examined its binding to serum albumin and its metabolites for doping control [16][17].

No studies found. No controlled human trial of methasterone has been published. Related literature consists of case reports of harm in supplement users [4][18], analyses of contaminated supplements [1][8], and laboratory metabolism and binding studies [14][16][19].

Documented harms come from case reports. A 2006 case report in the American Journal of Gastroenterology described cholestatic jaundice and IgA nephropathy after using Superdrol, which had been advertised as having no hormonal activity [18]. A 2009 case report and literature review described severe cholestasis with renal failure associated with its use [4]. A further case report discusses hepatitis-associated aplastic anemia [20]. An in vitro study of anabolic steroids and the bile acid enzyme AKR1D1 examined a possible route for liver effects of steroids as a group [21].

In a 2012-2013 New York cluster, about 16 residents reported fatigue, scalp hair loss and muscle aches after taking B-vitamin supplements that were later found to contain methasterone, dimethazine and methylstenbolone; one person was hospitalised with liver damage [8]. Forum posts describe other effects such as gynecomastia, lipid changes and suppressed natural testosterone, and recommend post-cycle therapy; these are community reports and not trial findings [22][2][23].

Methasterone was synthesised in the 1950s as an anabolic agent, according to the encyclopedia article drawn on here, and was never developed as a drug [3]. It reappeared on the supplement market in the early 2000s, a period in which analytical surveys showed supplements increasingly contaminated with or intentionally spiked with anabolic steroids, including newer designer steroids such as methasterone [1]. T Nation threads from 2005 discuss its sale as a supplement and question how it was legal [9][22]. Its later regulatory history involved US scheduling and placement on prohibited lists in sport [3][8].

A 2023 analysis described methasterone as a Schedule III controlled substance in the US [8]. It is prohibited in sport [3]. Products labelled as legal alternatives, such as methylstenbolone, have been found to contain it [15].

Methasterone is mentioned on looksmax.org in threads about oral steroid stacks and, in two threads started by self-described 14-year-olds, in the context of height. Replies there said the changes were due to puberty timing and that such compounds were more likely to limit height than add to it [24][25][26]. Other posters called it hepatotoxic and compared it with other orals [11].

lore.intro: Methasterone, mainly under the name Superdrol, appears in T Nation logs and looksmax.org discussions of oral anabolic steroids, often with comparisons to other orals and with warnings about liver effects [11][23][26].
